moves.headline: StoneX fell 27% after quarterly profit came in well below what analysts expected
moves.summary: StoneX reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $0.66 per share against roughly $0.92 expected. Revenue grew 12% but net income slipped 2% as interest and pay costs rose faster than revenue.
why: StoneX Group published results for its fiscal fourth quarter after the market closed on November 18. Net operating revenues rose 12% to $655.2 million, but net income fell 2% to $84.2 million and diluted earnings per share fell 6% to $0.66. Analysts had expected about $0.92, so the company missed by more than a quarter.

The reason profit did not follow revenue is visible in the cost lines. Interest expense rose 28% to $524 million and variable compensation rose 17%, both faster than revenue, and the share count was about 5% higher than a year earlier after the company’s largest acquisition. Return on equity fell to 11.6% from 15.2%.

The full year was a record — net income of $525.4 million, up 72% — and management stressed that the acquisition was integrated on schedule. The market looked instead at the direction of the latest quarter: a business whose earnings had been growing 50% or more for the year reported a decline in the most recent three months.
context: StoneX earns money from trading volumes, market volatility and the interest it earns on client balances. That makes its quarterly profit lumpier than a typical financial company’s. A miss of this size in a stock priced for continued fast growth produces an outsized move.
